sections.title: Plan H in 3D
sections.html:
Plan H in 3D

Your pick, revision 2 (more open ground, tents at the forecourt's edges, the boiler house under the stack, farmland off the west edge), traced into the kit: 0 errors, walkable in the 3D game. The made pieces carry over: the well, six full-size tents, the greenhouse (refitted larger, about 7.4 m tall) and the smokestack. Below, this grey-box painted by the isolated agent (step 3); I haven't looked at them.

  • Still to build: the glyph paths in the ground (from the well to everything, and along the road out); the broken wall's rubble (a regular flight stands in); the purifier on the jetty; the battery's boiler house (a grey box); lanterns on the road's far side; healing devices and triage dressing for the urgency; the vines.
  • To fix: the beach has the sea-wall balustrade along the water; the forecourt is plain paving with a stray wedge of grass on its south side; the old pipes are gone (glyph paths replace them).

sections.title: Your notes on plan H in 3D (round 3)
sections.html:
Your notes on plan H in 3D (round 3)

Done in the scene (free): the broken wall is gone, so the shore is one stair down and back; every tent turned so its open side faces the camera, each a few degrees off as if pitched in a hurry; crates, barrels and rope left on the paving round the tents; lamp posts on the road's far side. Still 0 errors.

sections.title: Round 2: four new plans
sections.html:
Round 2: four new plans

Your notes on the painted plan D sent the infirmary back to the plans stage, as the process asks. The new brief, from your notes: the well (which taps the magical field, not water) mainly feeds a grand greenhouse and the farmland beyond the wall; this morning's triage camp is thrown up round it, crowded and urgent, with healing devices; glowing glyph paths in the ground instead of pipes; one level where people gather; a Life-magic sea-water purifier on the shore; one built stair down, a broken wall's rubble back up; lanterns on the road out. Three plans that really differ, then the structure critic's recommended mix. The paintings were made by an isolated agent; I haven't looked at them. Plan D, shown to the critic blind, scored 4/10.

E: the broad terrace critic 5/10

One wide level for the arrival, the well, the camp and the greenhouse; all the height in the drop to a long shore. Roomy, but a box, and the greenhouse sits in the corner the camera sees least.

F: the crescent critic 7/10

The clifftop curves round a sheltered cove: the well at the apex, the camp along both arms, the greenhouse at the west tip, the road out from the east tip. Says what the place is, but the well sits on the narrowest strip, cramped again.

G: the prow critic 6/10

The well out on a prow over the sea, the camp on one flat level behind it. Fewest levels; but you cross the whole camp before the well, and the camp is a rectangle again.

H: the crescent with a forecourt the critic's mix

F with G's flat camp folded into its head: a broad forecourt about two screens wide where the arrival, the well and the busiest tents share one level; the cove pushed south; the purifier out on a jetty so it shows; the road out from the east arm. Drafted after the critic; not scored yet.

Which plan should the infirmary be built from?

My pick: H, the critic's mix: the crescent's outline and view across the cove, with the room you asked for where people gather.

Everything below this section is plan D, the layout these replace, kept for reference.

sections.title: Where it stands
sections.html:
Where it stands

Yes, the concept art and flow are done. The infirmary went through reading the concept, plans, flow and sense on 22 November as a flat grey-box. Today's work started the second half: building it in 3D.

Done · 22 Nov, as a grey-box

Deciding what the place is

  1. Concept art read as a plan (the caged well, the cots, the conduits)
  2. Three plans plus a control; you picked plan D ("the flow is very good, where you see the people to heal first")
  3. Flow in the game: 8/10, passed (four rounds, revisions 4 to 7)
  4. Sense in the game: 9/10, passed (revision 9)
Started · 26 Nov

Building it on the kit

  1. Trace plan D into a kit scene, 0 errors (today)
  2. Walkable in the 3D game (today, on its branch)
  3. Layout round 2: the stills moved, the east flight, the bath; a fresh critic approved it at 7.5/10, and its fixes are in
  4. Greenhouse, stills and tents modelled and placed (90 credits)
  5. Well, smokestack and bath dressing modelled and placed (120 credits; 210 in all)
  6. The pipes, drawn in code along their routes (free)
  7. The shore widened to six rows, with a sand beach (your note: "way too constrained")
  8. The painted layout against the concept (below), and the pipes; then the vines, flowers and smoke
  9. Surfaces: tiling textures from Codex
  10. Paint-over of the grey-box, as the dressing target
  11. Dressing: lamps, beds, cots, pipes, vines
  12. Beauty, judged in the whole scene at the game's camera

sections.title: From concept to scene
sections.html:
From concept to scene

The concept is a walled box. Plan D kept its ideas (the caged well, the conduits, the cots under tents) and put them on a slope down to the sea, with the road arriving from the north on the well's axis.

sections.title: The layout, painted
sections.html:
The layout, painted

The step we skipped: a Codex painting of the grey-box in the concept's style, keeping the layout, so you can compare it with the original concept before more pieces are made. An isolated agent painted these from the renders (with the wider shore); I haven't looked at them, as the process asks, so they're unjudged. Click to enlarge.

Does the layout hold up next to the concept?

The concept is a walled garden on one level round the well; plan D put it on a slope down to the sea, with the tents above and the shore below. If the painting loses what you liked in the concept, say what, and the layout changes before more pieces go in.

sections.title: What's off in this draft
sections.html:
What's off in this draft

  • The tent split gave three loose cots; the fourth cot, the table and the lantern are fused to the tent.
  • Living parts still to come: the vines on the well and pipes (drawing back as the well relights), flowers in the planters, the smokestack's smoke.
  • The conduit walkways (raised paths from the well to what it feeds) are gone from the layout; they come back in dressing as the brass pipes below.
  • The two big paved tiers look alike: they need different floors (the read asked for it) and the pipes to break them up. That's for the surfaces and dressing steps.
  • Woods are drawn as plain lawn: the kit has no woods floor yet. East of the stills, the top tier's wall ends in an earth bank where the woods start.

sections.title: The layout review
sections.html:
The layout review

You said a reviewer's approval would do for the layout. A fresh critic, given only the read, the principles, the plan and these renders, walked each pass as a first-time player.

  • Verdict: approve, 7.5/10 (the flat grey-box had 8). "Everything else carried over or got better, especially the shore bay."
  • Its one structural change: the first two-flight east descent "reads as a pen" and is "overbuilt" for a 1.5 m drop; make it one run along the wall face. Done: the render above is the fixed version.
  • Smaller fixes, done: the cobbles start at the well, the bath bay has a built back wall. Left for dressing: the tents need real footprints before the top tier's emptiness can be judged.

sections.title: The new pieces
sections.html:
The new pieces

Fourteen Codex pictures, two takes per piece, in the courtyard pieces' style (sandstone, blue and gold, brass). Each one becomes a Meshy model only after you pick it. Click any picture to enlarge it.

Round 1 picked: greenhouse a, stills a and tent a are being modelled now (about 90 credits). Round 2, for your OK: the well, pipes, smokestack and bath dressing, redone as structure only per your notes; about 30 credits each, about 120 for all four. The two sheets are split into parts after modelling.

The well, redone without vines (round 2)

Your note: structure only, the vines grown in the game so they can draw back as the well relights. My pick: b: the same cage as before, clean, and you can see where the pipes join. a lost the lattice cage.

The greenhouse

My pick: a, closest to the concept and best from our camera. It's about twice as long as it is wide; the fit step squashes it to its 7 × 6 m footprint.

The stills

My pick: a, the open shed from the concept, with more depth. Its banners carry a leaf, not the academy star; a quick Codex edit can swap that before modelling.

A tent with cots (four of them, in an arc)

My pick: a: four cots and open sides. b's closed back would hide the cots from some camera angles.

The conduit pipes, redone without vines (round 2)

My pick: b, over the picture agent's a: the three-quarter view gives Meshy depth to work from, and the open pipe mouths join better. Both split cleanly. Both put a fleur-de-lis on the blue band, not the academy star; it's a few pixels at the game camera, but say if you want it swapped first (a free Codex edit).

The battery's smokestack, redone without smoke (round 2)

My pick: b: the same design, and the three-quarter view gives Meshy both faces of a square stack. The smoke will be an effect rising from the flue.

Bath dressing, redone: empty pots, urns, towel stand, no stairs (round 2)

Both have three empty planters (round, square, a long trough) for flowers grown in the game, two urns and a towel stand. My pick: b: more depth, and one fewer part to split.

sections.title: The pipes
sections.html:
The pipes

Meshy fused the pipe sheet into one object (left), so the pipes are now drawn in code along their routes, like the kerbs and road stones (your pick): brass tube, riveted collars, blue bands with the academy star, sandstone saddles, T-joints, climbs down walls and open mouths, with painted textures from Codex. They don't block walking.

In the infirmary they run from the well's three stubs: west to the greenhouse, east to the stills, north up the overlook wall to a T feeding both tents, and south across the well's tier and down the bath bay's wall to an open mouth over the pool (the overlook and shore views above). The south pipe crosses the middle of the well's tier; it could run along an edge instead if it cuts the space up.

Do the pipes work?

sections.title: The purifier, camp kit and boiler house pictures (round 3)
sections.html:
The purifier, camp kit and boiler house pictures (round 3)

New pictures from Codex for your OK before any Meshy model (structure only). About 30 credits each if all three go ahead, 90 in all; the camp kit is one sheet split into six props.

The purifier, painted into the cove (your note: leaning to C, more concepts, hard to picture in the scene)

Six ideas, each painted into this cove at the game camera, with the structure on its own beside it for modelling. None is a cage, crystal or dome.

My pick: 2: your C, made part of the cove: the drum anchors the jetty from the beach, and from the forecourt you see the tower's top where the glyph path arrives. 6 is the most readable "lifting the sea up to the greenhouse", but the screw needs animating.

Tent-building materials to strew round the camp (one sheet, split)

My pick: b: strapped poles, rolled canvas with the star trim, stakes and a mallet, a stretcher laid flat, blankets, an open crate of bandages: looks in use. Its blankets are cream, not blue.

The battery's boiler house, beside the smokestack

My pick: a: brick on a sandstone plinth, the stack's band of stars under the eaves, open doors onto a boiler, coal bays. (b bakes glowing windows into the picture.)

sections.title: Round 6: the purifier, built
sections.html:
Round 6: the purifier, built

Your pick, idea 2, modelled in one Meshy call (30 credits; 300 this session, 1,164 left) and split into its two parts: the settling drum stands in the sea as the jetty's head; the pump tower stands on the beach in a bay cut into the cliff, its top above the forecourt where the glyph path will arrive; a brass pipe runs along the jetty between them. Also merged main again (PR #31) and re-laid the court's stones, as issue #30 advised. 0 errors.

sections.title: Healing devices, round 1: your answers
sections.html:
Healing devices, round 1: your answers

Healing devices for the camp, where each glyph path ends by the tents: Codex pictures for your pick before any Meshy model (about 30 credits each). Several takes include a cot only for scale; the model would be the device alone.

A healing lamp over a cot

My pick: a: a brass tripod holding a Life-rune bowl over the patient, a rune plate at its foot where the path ends. (b reads as a crystal brazier.)

A mender's pylon serving two cots

My pick: a: a post between two cots with brass arms out over them and a rune plate at its foot. (b reads as a desk lamp.)

A rune frame over a stretcher

My pick: b: a brass camp-bed frame under a hinged lid of rune tiles, a hose to a rune stake: portable and clearly powered.

Triage dressing (one sheet, split)

My pick: b: buckets, a washstand, a camp stool, an instrument table, an open chest of bottles, a lantern post, a rack of worn cloaks: more triage story.

  • Your answers: the lamp per bed is too busy; lamp b's look suits one station per tent; the pylon could serve two beds instead; the frame would hide the patient, so instead a small emitter behind each pillow, wired to the tent's station, which is wired to the well. Round 2 pictures of that system go on the front tab. The triage sheet (b) is being modelled.

sections.title: Round 4: the weathered floor, the boiler house, the camp kit
sections.html:
Round 4: the weathered floor, the boiler house, the camp kit

A new floor, weathered, laid stone by stone with the courtyard's method (main's paving update merged in first): worn flagstones and cobbles in wide joints, chipped edges, stains, moss over the rims, grass and earth in the joints, missing stones and packed-earth patches, the paving breaking up into the lawn at its edges. The courtyard keeps its look and can use it later. The boiler house (a) and the camp kit (b) are modelled (60 credits; 270 this session, 1,194 left) and placed: stretchers and medical crates where the triage is, poles, canvas and stakes dropped between the tents. 0 errors; all 724 tests pass.

  • Floor, still rough: where rows of stones from different edges meet, the big stones form crazy-paving patches (beside the well); the narrow road is very broken; the lawn texture is a bright lime next to the concept's softer grass.
  • The camp props read small at the game camera: they're real-world size. The courtyard's paint-overs drew such things about twice life size; I can scale them up if you agree.

sections.title: Round 5: foliage, a softer meadow, bigger props
sections.html:
Round 5: foliage, a softer meadow, bigger props

Your notes: you like the stone pattern (kept); the lawn was rough; way more foliage; props bigger. The camp props are 1.8x life size now (a rule on the veto list). A new softer, varied grass, meadow (Codex tiles, less saturated, drifting warm and cool, darker under trees), the weathered paving fraying into it. Foliage grown in code: birches, cherries, wisteria, yellow bushes in a wood along the north and east edges; shrubs, lavender and meadow flowers round the forecourt's edges and between the tents, the middle round the well left open; planting on the cliff top and in the cove's corners, vines over the parapets and cove walls; six crop fields to the west running off the map. The courtyard's lawn unchanged. 0 errors, 724 tests pass.

  • Still rough: birches are plain pale trunks, the wisteria tree reads as a round lilac shrub rather than hanging blossom; few vines on the middle cove cliff; the fields a bit bright with hard edges; shrubs up close are lumpy.

sections.title: The glyph paths (round 7)
sections.html:
The glyph paths (round 7)

The glyph paths are a new kit feature: carved rune lines flush with the floor (you walk over them), glowing Life green with a slow pulse running out from the well, pads at their ends, medallions at bends and joins; each line can be set lit, dim or dark, so the fix can relight them one by one later. In the infirmary they run from the well to the greenhouse and the fields, to each pair of tents, and to the cliff top above the purifier's tower (only to things that use the well's power; the line along the road out was dropped). They replace the pipes (the purifier keeps its own pipe on the jetty). 0 errors.

sections.title: Round 8: the well's vines and the stack's smoke
sections.html:
Round 8: the well's vines and the stack's smoke

Both grown in code, not baked into the models (your rule). Thorny vines with leaves and white and yellow flowers wind round the well's cage and the crystal and lie across the first stretch of each glyph path. The game can draw them back while it runs: each vine withers from its tip, its leaves browning and dropping, down to stumps at the foot, so the fix can show the recovery (and a path's own vines can be cut as it relights). The smoke is a soft stylised plume rising from the stack's flue and drifting on the wind. 724 tests pass.

Your note on the purifier: the pipe on the jetty looked unconnected and like it would block. It's gone: the tower's own downpipe meets the beach and the link to the drum runs under the jetty, implied. The jetty is clear to walk.

  • Rough: fully choked, the crystal is nearly hidden (it shows clearly at half); the stems are plain up close; the smoke's puffs can swap order as they loop (hard to see).
